Building libsurface

A hand-kept Makefile, no build system to configure. You need a C11 compiler and make. Nothing else: no library outside libc and libm.

make                          # libsurface.a
make test                     # the unit suite, the same command CI runs
make shared                   # libsurface.so, as the packages build it
make install PREFIX=/usr/local [DESTDIR=...]
make clean

The code is plain C11 built with -Wall -Wextra -Werror, so a warning is a build failure. CC and CFLAGS can be overridden on the command line; the warning flags are kept even then.

make install copies the header to $(PREFIX)/include/surface/, the archive to $(PREFIX)/lib (LIBDIR= to change it) and a pkg-config file, so a consumer builds with:

cc app.c $(pkg-config --cflags --libs libsurface)

(--static adds libm for a link against the archive.)

Tests

Every test runs through tests/run-test.sh, which gives it a timeout: a hang is a failure, never a stalled build. A test that exits 77 proved this machine cannot host it and is reported as SKIP, never as a pass.

The suites need no device. tests/harness.h is a fake backend that records every write, a fake host that answers the surface's moves the way a console does (echoing at once, lagging, or refusing), and a virtual clock that runs the surface's timers in order:

  • test_motor: the motor policy, case by case as the X-Touch driver's suite proved it;
  • test_audit: the motor-law audit of 2026-09-25 and the fast-throw round trip;
  • test_bank: the bank window;
  • test_meter: meter ballistics, ring rendering, and the step law against tests/golden/meter-steps.txt, vectors generated once from the TypeScript law and fixed;
  • test_c24: the Control|24's rules: release debounce, set-point echo, the replay on every session.

The script checks: constants-check.sh (each timing constant declared once, in the header), conformance-packaging.sh (the version and soname agree in every packaging copy), test_install.sh (a consumer builds against an installed tree through pkg-config alone), test_workflows.sh (the workflows parse), and public-sources-check.sh with its own test.

The DigiNet module

libsurface-diginet and tools/surface-c24 need libdiginet with the desk mux (diginet/transport/diginet_mux.h, libdiginet 0.1.4 and later). DIGINET says what to do:

make                                   # DIGINET=auto: the module when libdiginet is found, else a SKIP line
make DIGINET=yes                       # the module, or a failed build (the packages)
make DIGINET=no                        # the core alone
make DIGINET_SRC=../libdiginet         # libdiginet from a built source tree instead of pkg-config
make DIGINET_SRC=../libdiginet test    # + the module's tests

A source tree is linked from its archives, into the shared library too: that is for working on the two together, never for a package. make shared adds libsurface-diginet.so (its own soname, SURFACE_DIGINET_ABI) and surface-c24 linked to it; make install adds the header, libsurface-diginet.pc and the tool.

surface-c24's default helper is DIGINET_SRC's tools/diginet-packet-helper, else diginet-packet-helper in PATH (SURFACE_C24_HELPER= builds it to look in PATH always, as the packages do; --helper PATH overrides either at run time). The helper needs setcap cap_net_raw+ep (libdiginet's docs/diginet-packet-helper.1).

The module's tests, in tests/diginet/, run after the core's:

  • test_diginet: the module against libdiginet's desk emulator, in process, on a virtual clock: the board replayed on every ONLINE; each report of a touched cap echoed as its set-point, and once more at the release with no snap; a host move on an untouched cap and never on a touched one; the inputs; a deaf desk and a foreign session as warnings; the repaint after a desk restart and at the first announce after a host restart; a desk that goes and comes back;
  • test_c24_tool: surface-c24 itself, unprivileged, its socket from diginet-packet-helper, against the emulator on a veth pair in a user and network namespace of the test's own. SKIP with no helper or no such namespace;
  • test_install.sh: the module installed, a consumer built through pkg-config alone;
  • emu-sync-check.sh: libdiginet installs no test code, so its emulator is copied into tests/diginet/ (tests/diginet/SOURCE); this holds the copies to the DIGINET_SRC tree.

The Mackie module

libsurface-mackie is built when libmackie is found: through pkg-config, or from a built tree with MACKIE_SRC=../libmackie. MACKIE=auto (the default) builds it when found, MACKIE=yes stops the build when not, MACKIE=no never builds it. make test runs tests/mackie/test_mackie when it is built, and says SKIP when it is not.
